title: Keep one item, never look ahead
hook: You can hold one item and can't see how long the stream is. Who ends up kept?

doesNotKnow: that you can pick a uniform random item from a stream of unknown length in one pass

misconception: To choose a fair item from a stream you must store the whole stream first, or favour early items.
objective: The learner can explain that replacing the kept item with item i at chance 1/i leaves every item with the same final chance, because item 1 survives 1/2 x 2/3 x 3/4 = 1/4 and each later item has a smaller chance to get in but fewer draws to survive.

claims.text: With the rule 'item i replaces the kept one with chance 1/i', item 1 survives a 4-item stream with chance 1/2 x 2/3 x 3/4 = 1/4.
claims.source: Item 1 is still kept after arrival i exactly when draw i fails, chance 1 - 1/i = (i - 1)/i; the draws are independent, so the product for i = 2, 3, 4 is 1/2 x 2/3 x 3/4 = 1/4. Builder's node script (2026-10-14, algo2-sc) reproduces the exact distribution. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own node exact distribution: item 1 survives 1/2 x 2/3 x 3/4 = 1/4; stage CHAIN builds '1 x 1/2 x 2/3 x 3/4'; reveal matches.

claims.text: After i items have arrived, every one of them is the kept item with chance exactly 1/i, so after 4 every bar is at 1/4.
claims.source: Induction: if each of items 1..i-1 is kept with chance 1/(i-1), then after arrival i item i is kept with chance 1/i and each older item with 1/(i-1) x (i-1)/i = 1/i. Builder's exact enumeration: after 2 [1/2, 1/2], after 3 [1/3 x3], after 4 [1/4 x4]. The stage bars are computed from this, not simulated. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own node exact enumeration: after 2 [1/2,1/2], after 3 [1/3 x3], after 4 [1/4 x4]; stage bars are 1/k for arrived items (computed, not simulated).

claims.text: Item 3 got in with chance 1/3 and then stays with chance 3/4 after 4 items (3/5 after 5): each later item had a smaller chance to get in, but fewer draws left to survive. Every bar reached 1/4 at item 4.
claims.source: Item i enters with chance 1/i (smaller for larger i) and must then survive draws i+1..n, with chance i/n; the product is 1/n for every i. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Derivation holds: entry 1/i times survival i/n = 1/n; reveal sentence matches. | REWORDED v2 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14): v2 shows each item's two factors under its bar (gets in 1/i x stays i/k), so item 3's 1/3 x 3/4 is drawn, not told. Unverified. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24): VERIFIED. Entry 1/i x survival i/k = 1/k re-derived; own node exact distribution: every bar 1/4 at k=4, 1/5 at k=5. Reveal can only open at k=5 (milestone fifth), so it says 'stays with 3/5', which the claim's parenthesis covers; the 1/4 dashes stay on stage.

claims.text: 1,000 seeded streams (seed 1) of 4 kept items 1 to 4 236, 250, 257 and 257 times; 1,000 seeded streams of 5 kept items 1 to 5 195, 197, 191, 214 and 203 times.
claims.source: Builder's node script and TALLY in Demo.tsx: mulberry32(1), 1,000 streams, draw rng() < 1/i for i = 2, 3, 4. The reveal and stage quote the TALLY constant, not hard-coded numbers. Expected about 250 each, standard deviation about 13.7. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own re-implementation of mulberry32(1) with Demo.tsx loop: TALLY 236, 250, 257, 257; chi-square 1.18; SD sqrt(1000 x 1/4 x 3/4) = 13.7. Reveal and stage quote TALLY. | REWORDED v2 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14): v2: the run uses the current length (4, or 5 after 'A 5th item arrives'); the reveal quotes the tally drawn on stage. Builder's node replay of tally(4) and tally(5) with mulberry32(1). Seed 1 is the v1 seed, not chosen for the result. Unverified. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24): VERIFIED. Own node replay of tally(n) with mulberry32(1) (copied from src/kit/random.ts): tally(4) = 236, 250, 257, 257; tally(5) = 195, 197, 191, 214, 203. Reveal always quotes TALLY[5] (k = 5 at reveal); stage shows TALLY[4] if run at k = 4. Minor, not a fact error: the tally switches from TALLY[4] to TALLY[5] when the 5th item arrives without a re-run.

claims.text: The shown stream uses seed 1: item 2 draws 0.627 (kept item stays 1), item 3 draws 0.003 (replaces it), item 4 draws 0.527 (item 3 stays), item 5 draws 0.981 (item 3 stays).
claims.source: Disclosed seed (pattern disclose-chosen-seeds): seed 1 was the first seed tried and was not selected for its result. The spec's placeholder seed 7 was rejected because its tallies (257, 247, 249, 247; chi-square 0.27) look flatter than a typical run. Seed 1's chi-square is 1.18; across seeds 1-200 the median is 2.41 (builder's node script). The 1,000 streams start from the same seed, so the shown stream is the first of them. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own node: seed 1 draws 0.627 (keep 1), 0.003 (keep 3), 0.527 (keep 3); stage shows 'seed 1'. Seed 7 tallies 257, 247, 249, 247 (chi-square 0.27) reproduce. Minor: my median chi-square over seeds 1-200 is 2.39, not 2.41 (source text only; not learner-facing). | REWORDED v2 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14): v2 adds item 5's draw (4th mulberry32(1) value = 0.981, not under 1/5). Builder's node run. Unverified. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24): VERIFIED. Own node: mulberry32(1) draws 0.627 (keep 1), 0.003 (< 1/3, keep 3), 0.527 (keep 3), 0.981 (not < 1/5, keep 3); stage line 'Item 5: draw 0.981, needs under 1/5: keep item 3'.

claims.text: Then a 5th item came, and the same rule took every bar to 1/5. It held one item in memory and never needed to know the length.
claims.source: The state is the kept item and the count i of items seen; each step uses only i and the new item. Algorithm R with a reservoir of size 1: Vitter 1985, 'Random sampling with a reservoir', ACM TOMS 11(1); Knuth, TAOCP vol. 2, section 3.4.2 (citations from memory, not opened; check before publishing). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Holds from the code (state = kept item + count). Vitter, 'Random sampling with a reservoir', ACM TOMS 11(1):37-57, March 1985 confirmed by search-result text only (dl.acm.org blocked); Knuth TAOCP vol. 2 sec. 3.4.2 (Algorithm R) not opened, from my own knowledge. Learner sentence does not depend on either. | REWORDED v2 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14): v2 adds the 5th-item step: after k arrivals each item has chance 1/k (c2's argument with k = 5); the rule uses only i and one stored item. Unverified. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24): VERIFIED. Holds from the code: the rule uses only i and one stored item; at k = 5 every bar is 1/5 (own exact enumeration). Learner sentence rests on the derivation, not on Vitter/Knuth (not opened).

claims.text: Under each bar: item i gets in with chance 1/i and then stays with chance i/k after k items, so every item's chance is 1/k (for example item 2 after 4: 1/2 x 2/4).
claims.source: Item i enters with 1/i; it survives arrivals i+1..k with (i/(i+1)) x ... x ((k-1)/k) = i/k (telescoping product). 1/i x i/k = 1/k. Drawn unreduced as frac(1,i) x frac(i,k) in Demo.tsx v2. Builder, 2026-10-14. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24): VERIFIED. Telescoping product (i/(i+1)) x ... x ((k-1)/k) = i/k re-derived; Demo draws frac(1,i) x frac(i,k), e.g. '1/2 x 2/4' for item 2 at k = 4 (item k shows '1/k x 1').

recall.question: Keeping one item from a stream, you replace it with item i at chance 1/i. With 10 items, what is item 1's final chance?
recall.why: Item 1 survives 1/2 x 2/3 x ... x 9/10 = 1/10; the product telescopes, so every item ends with 1/n.
